doc.citation: Wellman, C.H., Steemans, P. and Miller, M.A. (2015). Spore assemblages from Upper Ordovician and lowermost Silurian sediments recovered from the Qusaiba-1 shallow core hole, Qasim region, central Saudi Arabia. Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology 212, 111–126.
doc.comment: Table 2 records 293 presences in 37 samples; captions add 12 presences, including three otherwise unlisted depths. Table 2 prints depths with m, whereas Fig. 3, descriptions and captions use ft; units and anomalous depths are retained without correction. Illustrated means illustrated from the particular sample. Author-year and spelling inconsistencies occur, including Sphaerosaccus/Sphaerasaccus. Section 2 gives early Katian for the oldest samples, whereas §6.1 gives mid-Katian; sample-level biozone boundaries are not supplied. Section 5 names Qalibah, although Table 2 contains only Sarah and Qasim samples; its qualitative formation-level report is flagged separately. Sarah reworking is demonstrated principally by marine palynomorphs, without identifying individual reworked spores. Material was previously reported by Steemans et al. (2009), Origin and radiation of the earliest vascular land plants, and in Steemans et al. (2008) and Wellman et al. (2008) abstracts.

items.age_basis_detail: Graptolite and palynological evidence. Section 2 describes possibly early Rhuddanian at 257–254.5 ft followed by mid-Aeronian at 254.5–231 ft; these are contextual intervals, not identified spore samples.
items.notes: Unresolved formation-name inconsistency: §5 explicitly describes assemblages from throughout the Qalibah Formation as essentially identical, referring to Table 2, but that table contains only Qasim and Sarah samples. The description lists cryptospore monads, dyads and tetrads, physically dissociated cryptospores, two hilate taxa and eight trilete taxa; naturally separating spores comprise less than 1% of the spore assemblage. No named taxon can be securely assigned specifically to a Qalibah sample from the supplied distribution table. This qualitative report is retained with an empty occurrence list rather than transferring the pooled taxonomic list to Silurian strata.
